pages.title: The Morning
pages.content:
The Morning

The Morning

Every company screening morning at Asaoka Screening is organized to provide a calm, orderly health check without unnecessary delay. From arrival at 7:30 to departures by 11:30, our clinical staff ensure each stage proceeds smoothly.

What to bring

Fasting from 21:00

Water is fine

Last year’s booklet, if you have one. Everything else is provided.

Schedule

Arrival and Morning Schedule

Staff arrive together at our clinic at 14 Linden Row at 7:30, where our reception team welcomes everyone and verifies their details. The entire screening cycle is arranged to conclude by 11:30, allowing employees to return to their normal routines with minimal disruption. Rather than waiting in crowded corridors, participants move through quiet, daylight-filled rooms where each test is ready as they arrive. Head nurse Lena Marsh coordinates the progression between departments so that individual waiting times remain short. Because our facility accepts between 5 and 40 staff per morning session, the atmosphere remains unhurried and personal throughout the four-hour visit. Staff complete all essential clinical assessments in a single morning.

Timing

How the morning runs

  • 7:30Arrival

    Check in together at the ground-floor reception desk; details are verified and the first stations are ready.

  • 7:45Blood & urine

    Fasting samples are collected first, so water is the only thing to have before this point.

  • 8:30Measurements, X-ray, ECG

    Height, weight and vision, then the low-dose chest X-ray and the resting ECG, in whatever order the rooms are free.

  • 10:30Consultation

    A private conversation with a physician about the morning and any immediate questions.

  • 11:30Leave

    Each person takes home a one-page same-day summary and a note on what happens next.

Preparation

Preparation and Fasting Requirements

To maintain the analytical accuracy of blood and urine samples, all attending employees must begin fasting from 21:00 on the evening prior to their appointment. Plain water is permitted during the morning, but coffee, tea, and breakfast should be avoided until laboratory samples have been collected. We also ask participants to bring last year's booklet if they have previously completed a check with us or another clinic. Having prior health records enables our physicians to identify physiological trends and evaluate changes over time. Once fasting samples are collected by laboratory technician Kai Lindqvist, employees may enjoy water while completing the remaining non-fasting stations.

Checks

The Five Core Clinical Checks

Body measurements & visionabout 15 min Blood & urineabout 10 min Chest X-rayabout 10 min ECGabout 10 min Physician consultationabout 15 min

Checks

The morning covers five focused clinical evaluations designed for thorough preventive care. First, nursing staff complete body measurements and vision screening to record baseline metrics. Second, Kai Lindqvist processes blood and urine samples in our laboratory. Third, Dr Tomás Riedel conducts a low-dose chest X-ray to examine respiratory and thoracic structures. Fourth, Dr Amara Okafor oversees a resting electrocardiogram (ECG) to monitor cardiovascular rhythm and electrical activity. Finally, each employee sits down for a private physician consultation with Dr Hana Asaoka to discuss general wellbeing and answer immediate health questions. Each examination takes place in a quiet, private consultation room.

Departure

Same-Day Summary and Departure

How results work

Before leaving at 11:30, every employee receives a preliminary same-day summary outlining immediate clinical observations. This immediate debriefing provides peace of mind before the complete laboratory analysis is finalized. Should any urgent health concerns arise during the morning, our physicians discuss them directly and privately with the employee before departure. For all standard screenings, detailed analytical booklets are prepared and posted within 10 working days. Employees leave our Harbour District clinic with clear guidance on subsequent steps, having completed their entire statutory annual health assessment in a calm, structured four-hour morning.

pages.title: Results & Follow-up
pages.content:
Results

Results & Follow-up

We believe diagnostic health checks are only as valuable as the clarity with which results are communicated. Our four-stage results pathway ensures employees understand their findings while maintaining strict workplace confidentiality.

Booklets by post

10 working days

Printed

Posted to each person, with a 20-minute explanation to follow.

Pathway

The Four-Stage Results Pathway

Our reporting follows four distinct, structured steps. First, each staff member receives a same-day summary before leaving at 11:30, providing immediate reassurance on primary observations. Second, our laboratory compiles all blood, urine, imaging, and cardiological data into an individualized printed booklet posted within 10 working days. Third, each employee attends a dedicated 20-minute explanation with a physician to review findings line by line. Fourth, if any result warrants specialist investigation, Dr Hana Asaoka or our clinical team provides a formal referral letter directly to the employee. This structured journey ensures continuous, clear medical guidance.

  • Same dayBefore you leave

    A nurse hands each person a one-page summary of the morning’s measurements, so nobody waits weeks to hear whether something stood out.

  • Printed bookletWithin 10 working days

    Every result is printed in a plain booklet with the reference range beside each number and posted to the person, not to the company.

  • 20-minute explanationMon–Fri 14:00–17:00

    A physician goes through the booklet with each person, in the centre or by phone, and answers questions in ordinary words.

  • Referral letterWhen needed

    Where a result deserves a closer look, we write a referral letter to the person’s own doctor or to a specialist.

Booklet

The Printed Results Booklet

Within 10 working days of the morning check, each participant receives an individualized printed booklet bound in high-grade format. Results nurse Mei Chen oversees the compilation of these booklets, ensuring that numerical readings are paired with clear reference ranges and plain-language interpretations. Historical data from previous years is placed alongside current metrics to show multi-year health trajectories clearly. Blood profiles, liver enzymes, kidney indicators, and cardiovascular metrics are displayed in accessible charts. This comprehensive physical document serves as a permanent, reliable personal medical record that employees can keep and share with their personal physicians.

Privacy

Employee Confidentiality and Employer Reporting

We maintain rigorous boundaries between individual medical data and corporate management. The employer receives only a high-level fit-for-work summary indicating employee attendance and general occupational fitness. Granular diagnostic findings, laboratory markers, chest X-rays, and ECG recordings remain strictly confidential between the employee and our medical team. Results are never disclosed to company management or human resources personnel without explicit written consent. This clear separation fosters trust, encouraging staff members to discuss health questions candidly during their private 20-minute consultation with our doctors.

Questions about your results?

Our results nurse and physicians are available on weekday afternoons from 14:00 to 17:00.

Contact the team

Physicians

Medical Leadership and Physicians

Dr Hana Asaoka founded Asaoka Screening in 2009 to create a calm, dignified environment for preventive medicine. Working alongside her is Dr Tomás Riedel, our radiologist, who oversees all chest X-ray evaluations with a focus on low-dose precision. Kai Lindqvist manages our on-site laboratory, processing blood and urine specimens immediately following morning collections to provide dependable analytical precision. pages.title: FAQ
pages.content:
FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

Here are clear answers to the most common questions regarding our corporate screening schedules, preparation protocols, and reporting procedures. If your company requires further details, please reach out to our team.

Questions

Eight common questions

  • Q1

    What are the hours for morning health checks and afternoon consultations?

    Health screening mornings take place from Monday through Saturday between 7:30 and 11:30. All participating staff members arrive together at 7:30 to complete their scheduled assessments before departing at 11:30. Afternoon result explanations and one-on-one doctor discussions are scheduled Monday through Friday between 14:00 and 17:00. These dedicated afternoon sessions ensure individual reviews never conflict with morning screening procedures. The clinic is closed on Sundays and all public holidays.

  • Q2

    How should employees prepare before arriving for their morning screening?

    All attending staff must fast starting from 21:00 on the evening prior to their morning check. While plain water is encouraged to stay hydrated, employees must avoid eating breakfast, juices, milk, tea, or coffee before their laboratory tests are completed. In addition, employees should bring last year's results booklet if they have one available. Prior records allow our physicians to assess long-term physical trends and compare blood markers accurately during the consultation.

  • Q3

    What group sizes can Asaoka Screening accommodate for company bookings?

    Our facility accommodates corporate cohorts ranging from a minimum of 5 staff up to a maximum of 40 staff per morning session. We require companies to reserve their screening dates at least 3 weeks in advance so our laboratory and medical staff can prepare individual files. Accommodating up to 40 participants ensures our team can deliver unhurried, attentive clinical care while maintaining a quiet, supportive clinic atmosphere.

  • Q4

    Which five clinical examinations are included during the screening morning?

    Every comprehensive screening morning covers five core clinical evaluations: body measurements and vision screening, blood and urine analysis, a low-dose chest X-ray, a resting electrocardiogram (ECG), and a private consultation with a physician. These five diagnostic checks provide a robust overview of metabolic, respiratory, cardiovascular, and general physical wellbeing. Each check is conducted in a private, quiet room by dedicated clinical specialists including Dr Hana Asaoka, Dr Tomás Riedel, and Dr Amara Okafor.

  • Q5

    When and how are medical results delivered to employees?

    Employees receive a preliminary same-day summary of basic observations before leaving our clinic at 11:30. Complete diagnostic findings are compiled into an individualized, printed booklet posted to the participant within 10 working days. Following receipt of the booklet, each employee attends a private 20-minute explanation session with a physician during our weekday afternoon hours (14:00 to 17:00) to review their findings and ask questions in complete confidence.

  • Q6

    What information from the health screening is shared with the employer?

    We uphold rigorous medical privacy standards. Employers receive solely an administrative fit-for-work summary indicating employee attendance and occupational clearance. Detailed diagnostic data, blood and urine test values, chest X-rays, and individual doctor notes remain strictly confidential between the employee and our clinical team. No confidential personal medical information is ever released to company management or human resources without explicit written authorization from the individual staff member.

  • Q7

    What packages and pricing options are available for company screenings?

    We offer four transparent core packages: the Essential check (€145), the Standard employee medical (€210), the Extended check with abdominal ultrasound (€320), and the Over-40 comprehensive assessment (€410). In addition, employers may add an eye pressure test for €25 or a hearing test for €20 per person. All quoted prices are per person, include VAT, and are consolidated onto a single corporate invoice without hidden administrative surcharges.

  • Q8

    What happens if an employee requires further medical follow-up or treatment?

    If a screening examination reveals an irregular diagnostic marker or clinical finding requiring secondary care, our physicians provide a formal referral letter during the 20-minute explanation session. Dr Hana Asaoka or our attending doctors explain the clinical context clearly and supply full laboratory notes for the employee's chosen specialist or family physician. This ensures seamless continuity of medical care without causing undue alarm or administrative delays.

Still have a question?

Our company liaison answers enquiries on weekdays.

Contact the team

posts.title: Rethinking the Company Medical: How a Calm Morning Protects Workplace Health
posts.excerpt: By replacing clinical friction with unhurried morning appointments and thorough physician explanations, corporate health screenings become an empowering annual routine for teams.
posts.content:
For many organizations, the annual employee medical has historically felt like an administrative hurdle rather than a genuine health benefit. Staff members often face crowded hospital waiting rooms, confusing clinical instructions, and weeks of uncertain waiting for opaque laboratory printouts. When health checks feel stressful or disjointed, employees view them with apprehension, and corporate managers struggle to coordinate attendance. When Dr Hana Asaoka founded Asaoka Screening in 2009 at 14 Linden Row in Harbour District, the objective was to fundamentally rethink this experience. A workplace health check should be an ordinary, calm morning embedded in everyday life, conducted with dignity, precision, and absolute respect for everyone's time.

The foundation of a calm screening lies in thoughtful scheduling and human scale. Serving 140 companies each year, our clinic limits morning cohorts to between 5 and 40 staff members. Operating Monday through Saturday from 7:30 to 11:30, the entire screening experience is contained within a four-hour window that allows employees to complete their checks and return to their work or personal routines without lingering fatigue. Staff arrive together at 7:30 after fasting from 21:00 the previous evening, bringing their previous year's booklet to establish long-term clinical continuity. From the reception desk to quiet examination rooms filled with soft morning light, head nurse Lena Marsh and the clinical team ensure that movement between diagnostic stations remains continuous and unhurried.

Within this focused morning, our medical team conducts five essential checks that establish a clear picture of employee health. Body measurements and vision screening provide foundational physical metrics. In the laboratory, Kai Lindqvist analyzes blood and urine samples to identify metabolic and biochemical markers. Dr Tomás Riedel conducts low-dose chest X-rays to assess thoracic and respiratory condition, while Dr Amara Okafor reviews resting electrocardiograms (ECG) to monitor cardiac rhythm. The morning concludes with a private consultation with Dr Hana Asaoka, where staff can discuss immediate concerns. Before departing at 11:30, each employee receives a preliminary same-day summary, removing immediate anxiety and providing peace of mind before detailed laboratory data is finalized.

The diagnostic journey continues well after the morning concludes through our structured results process. Within 10 working days, every participant receives a beautifully organized, printed results booklet compiled under the supervision of results nurse Mei Chen. Numerical values are placed within clear reference bands and compared against historical data, transforming clinical metrics into accessible personal insight. Furthermore, every employee attends a dedicated 20-minute explanation session with a physician during our afternoon hours between 14:00 and 17:00. This dedicated conversation gives staff the opportunity to understand what their numbers mean and discuss practical lifestyle adjustments in private. If secondary medical evaluation is warranted, our physicians provide a formal referral letter directly to the employee.

Equally critical to the success of corporate screening is the strict protection of employee privacy. Company management receives solely an administrative fit-for-work summary confirming attendance and general fitness. Detailed diagnostic markers, imaging records, and physician notes remain confidential between the individual and our medical team. This clear ethical boundary builds lasting trust across diverse workplaces, from the 12 designers at Fernhill Design Studio and the 28 active shift workers at Corran Bakery Wholesale to the 8 professionals at Oduya & Pell Accountants.
